messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testInfiniteLoop()` failed due to an infinite loop bug in the `HelpFormatter` class when printing help messages. The description of the bug explains that if there is not enough space to display a single word on one line (with a given width setting), `HelpFormatter` loops infinitely until the JVM crashes with OutOfMemoryError.

Looking at the related code in the stack:
- The test calls `HelpFormatter.printHelp(String, Options)`.
- This eventually calls the overloaded `printHelp` methods and reaches `printHelp(PrintWriter, int, String, String, Options, int, int, String, boolean)`.
- Within `printHelp`, it calls `printOptions` which delegates to `renderOptions`.
- `renderOptions` builds the option strings and their descriptions and calls `renderWrappedText` to wrap the text at the specified width.
- `renderWrappedText` uses a loop involving calls to `findWrapPos` to break the text into lines that fit the width.
- The infinite loop condition occurs when `findWrapPos` does not find a proper break position (`pos`) resulting in `pos` not changing between iterations.
- When `pos == lastPos` inside `renderWrappedText`, the code should throw a `RuntimeException` to avoid the infinite loop, but historically this may not have been present or correctly triggered in the reported version - leading to the hang (the comment mentions this is added "[CLI-162]").

Therefore, the root cause of the infinite loop bug is that when a word is longer than the allowed line width, the wrapping function cannot find a break position (`pos`) to split the word and either:
- fails to throw an exception, keeping the pos unchanged and looping endlessly, or
- fails to handle this edge case gracefully, leading to infinite looping.

The failing test verifies that such a long description setting causes this infinite loop hang. The presence of the check and exception in the code snapshot indicates this was a bug fixed by adding this guard clause.

None of the recent bug reports are directly relevant; the current report and test case directly target this infinite loop in wrapping long words.

Summary:
The infinite loop occurs inside `HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText` when wrapping long words that cannot fit the specified width. The loop fails to progress and eventually crashes the JVM before a safeguard exception was added. The tested fix introduces a runtime exception to prevent infinite loops by detecting unchanged wrap positions.

This matches the bug report details and the failure of `testInfiniteLoop()` which used a very narrow width (20) with a long word description causing the infinite loop before the fix.

Next, I can provide the best methods to fix this issue.
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer, int, int, java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
